answer: A slashable stake bond resists Sybils by charging every identity a deposit that is forfeited on fraud. Like a comet that burns fuel on each pass, an agent must lock funds before it can vote or attest; building a dune of ten thousand fake identities then means locking ten thousand bonds, while honest agents risk little because good work returns the stake. An atlas of past bonds and slashes is public, so a repeat offender's history follows it and verifiers can refuse fresh identities from wallets with a record of forfeiture. Attack cost scales linearly, honest cost stays flat.
